response_change.parent_relation: At fixed Vmax and Ki, the inhibitor effect on v_inh is fully determined by the ratio I/Ki, so all inhibitor-response curves across experimental conditions differ only through S in the standard competitive denominator Km*(1 + I/Ki) + S.
response_change.child_relation: Release the assumption of a fixed inhibitor affinity by allowing competitive binding strength to vary with an independently sampled environmental condition, so the rate depends on I and that condition jointly through an effective Ki; this rotates the inhibitor-response surface rather than only rescaling S dependence.
response_change.observable_effect: When substrate is held fixed and inhibitor is titrated under two environmental settings, the drop in rate with I becomes systematically steeper in one setting than the other, and one shared parent parameter set with fixed Ki cannot match both inhibitor-response curves simultaneously.

plan.activation_condition: Observable when inhibitor is in a regime comparable to its dissociation scale (I on the order of Ki) and the added environmental condition is varied enough to measurably shift apparent inhibitor affinity, with substrate held in a moderate unsaturated range S ~ Km so slope changes are visible.
plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, the mechanism appears as differing inhibitor-response steepness across sampled environmental settings; in holdout, the same affinity modulation extends to new combinations of substrate and inhibitor without changing the underlying competitive form.
plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent law when the environmental modulation of inhibitor affinity vanishes so the effective Ki becomes constant across all conditions.
plan.promotion_reason: With only S and I varied, the parent already uses the available inputs fully; making inhibitor affinity condition-dependent requires releasing one existing parameter as an independently varied experimental condition so the target mapping can change across environments rather than merely refitting constants.
plan.gap_statement: The current model assumes a single fixed competitive inhibitor dissociation constant across all assays, omitting realistic condition-dependent affinity changes such as pH- or ionic-strength-dependent inhibitor binding.
plan.baseline_assumption: Ki is constant and does not vary across assay conditions.
plan.scientific_mechanism: Environmental modulation of reversible inhibitor binding affinity at the active site, while competition with substrate remains mutually exclusive and catalysis still occurs only from the substrate-bound enzyme.
plan.rationale: Parent response relationship: at fixed substrate S, v_inh decreases monotonically with I with a slope entirely set by one shared constant Ki. The scientific gap is the fixed-environment assumption that inhibitor affinity does not change across assay conditions. A realistic next refinement is to let Ki vary as an independently sampled condition, representing environment-dependent competitive binding without altering the basic occupancy mechanism. Distinguishing condition: vary inhibitor concentration I while holding substrate S fixed near Km, and compare assays at two Ki conditions within an admissible range where I is comparable to each Ki. Then the child predicts different inhibitor-response steepness and curvature across those conditions because the effective competitive factor changes with Ki itself. A single parent parameter set cannot reproduce both curves simultaneously, since in the parent Ki is one constant shared across all observations. This is a genuine change in the scored target mapping, not merely an auxiliary reinterpretation. Limitation: if experiments never vary the environmental condition or if I is always far below Ki so inhibition is negligible, the refinement will not be observable.

contract.assumption_before: Ki is a fixed parameter shared by all assays.
contract.assumption_after: Ki varies across assay environments as a controlled condition while the competitive occupancy law itself is retained.
contract.parent_reduction: Fix Ki to a single constant value across all observations.

response_change.parent_relation: At fixed Ki, v_inh decreases with I through a linear competitive factor 1 + I/Ki, so the inhibitor effect versus I has one fixed curvature family across all assays.
response_change.child_relation: Replace the ideal dilute-solution dependence on inhibitor concentration with a non-ideal effective inhibitor activity that scales nonlinearly with I, so competition remains active-site exclusive but the apparent inhibition strength bends differently as I changes.
response_change.observable_effect: At fixed S and Ki, low-to-moderate I can show weaker-then-stronger or stronger-then-weaker incremental inhibition than the parent's single hyperbolic competitive form, while still remaining monotone and bounded.

plan.activation_condition: Observable when inhibitor titrations span a regime where solution nonideality is not negligible, typically I comparable to Ki and extending over at least several-fold concentration variation while S is held at sub-saturating to moderately saturating levels.
plan.train_hidden_contrast: Within training, differing curvature of v versus I appears across sampled Ki and S; in holdout, the same non-ideal activity effect becomes more evident at stronger inhibitor loads rather than introducing a qualitatively different mechanism.
plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent in the ideal-solution limit where inhibitor activity is proportional to concentration.
plan.gap_statement: The current model treats prepared inhibitor concentration as the effective binding-driving quantity, assuming ideal dilute behavior across the entire inhibitor titration.
plan.baseline_assumption: Free ligand concentrations are well approximated by prepared concentrations.
plan.scientific_mechanism: Non-ideal inhibitor activity in the assay medium modifies the concentration-to-occupancy mapping without changing the competitive active-site mechanism or catalytic competence assumptions.
plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the ideal-concentration assumption for inhibitor while keeping the same competitive occupancy picture. The parent target mapping has a fixed-environment shortcut: once Ki is chosen, changing I only moves the rate along one standard competitive curve governed by I/Ki. Hold S fixed and compare inhibitor titrations across assays where Ki is in the informative range and I sweeps from well below to comparable with Ki. The child allows the same monotone inhibition mechanism but with altered curvature in v versus I because effective inhibitor activity need not remain exactly proportional to prepared I. This changes the scored algebraic mapping itself, not merely an auxiliary trajectory. A single refit of Vmax and Km with the parent cannot reproduce assay-consistent departures in how inhibition strength accumulates across I when those departures are concentrated at higher inhibitor load but rates remain bounded below Vmax*S/(Km+S) and nonnegative. The effect is scientifically admissible in crowded or high-ionic-strength conditions, but may be weak if all sampled I values stay deep in the dilute ideal regime; in that limit the parent law is recovered.

plan.activation_condition: Observable when both substrate occupancy and inhibitor challenge are appreciable, e.g. S on the order of Km or larger and I on the order of Ki, so a substrate-dependent change in inhibitor potency is not masked by either negligible binding or complete saturation.
plan.train_hidden_contrast: Within training, low-S versus high-S inhibitor titrations can already show different apparent right-shifts or curvature; in holdout, the same mechanism extends to stronger substrate-loading regimes where the divergence grows systematically.
plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent law when the substrate-dependent modulation strength tends to zero, so inhibitor activity again depends only on I and Ki.
plan.gap_statement: The current model assumes assay-medium nonideality acts on inhibitor concentration alone and is unaffected by substrate loading, even though crowded or microenvironment-sensitive active-site access can make apparent inhibitor potency depend jointly on substrate and inhibitor levels.
plan.baseline_assumption: Relax the assumption that non-ideal inhibitor activity is a function of prepared inhibitor concentration only; instead, let the effective inhibitor term depend on the substrate environment as well while preserving mutually exclusive competition and catalysis only from ES.
plan.scientific_mechanism: Substrate-dependent modulation of apparent inhibitor binding/activity, such as active-site microenvironment or medium effects that alter inhibitor access or activity when substrate occupancy becomes substantial.
plan.rationale: Parent response relationship: v decreases monotonically with I at fixed S through a single I-dependent correction to competitive occupancy, and changing S mainly rescales competitive relief in the standard Michaelis-Menten way. Child change: the inhibitor-response surface gains a genuine S-I interaction because substrate-rich conditions alter apparent inhibitor potency, changing slope and curvature of v versus I differently across substrate slices. Distinguishing condition: vary I over values comparable to Ki while comparing low S<<Km to moderate/high S~Km or above, with Vmax, Km, Ki, and alpha held fixed across all conditions. Under these admissible conditions, the child predicts that inhibitor titrations at different S are not collapsible by the parent’s single shared I-only activity correction; apparent potency can weaken more strongly at high S than simple competitive displacement alone allows. This changes the scored algebraic mapping directly, not merely an auxiliary trajectory. Limitation: if all data lie at S<<Km or I<<Ki, the new interaction is weak and the parent may remain adequate.

plan.gap_statement: The current model assumes inhibitor activity presented to the active site remains effectively proportional to prepared inhibitor concentration, aside from the existing substrate-sensitive correction, even at very high inhibitor loading.
plan.baseline_assumption: Free ligand concentrations are well approximated by prepared concentrations, specifically using an effectively linear inhibitor concentration-to-activity mapping over the sampled range.
plan.scientific_mechanism: Assay-medium nonideality or inhibitor self-association causes the active inhibitor fraction to saturate with increasing prepared inhibitor concentration, reducing the incremental competitive effect of added inhibitor at high I.
plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the parent's fixed-environment assumption that prepared inhibitor concentration maps almost linearly to competitive activity over the whole assay range. Here the varied condition is I, with S and Ki held fixed across contrasted curves. The parent produces a single-phase inhibition curve whose high-I approach is fully determined by one Ki-scaled loading term times the substrate-dependent factor; after refitting one shared parameter set it cannot independently match both the initial inhibitory slope and an experimentally earlier high-I flattening across multiple S values if active inhibitor availability itself saturates. The child changes the target mapping itself, not just an auxiliary quantity: v_inh as a function of supplied I acquires stronger concave-down behavior, with less additional rate suppression per increment of I once I reaches the nonideal activity-saturation regime. This is scientifically admissible in concentrated inhibitor or crowded-medium conditions, while remaining monotone nonincreasing in I and bounded by Vmax. A limitation is that if all sampled I are well below the onset of inhibitor-activity saturation, the refinement becomes practically indistinguishable from the parent.

plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, moderate S sweeps may only show extra flattening relative to Michaelis saturation; in holdout extended to larger S, the same mechanism produces an actual downturn, extending the same substrate-loading effect rather than introducing a new process.
plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent law in the limit of vanishing substrate-inhibition strength or when all sampled S stay well below the substrate-inhibition scale.
plan.gap_statement: The current model assumes every substrate-bound enzyme molecule is equally productive regardless of how large the substrate concentration becomes, so substrate can only oppose inhibitor occupancy and never reduce catalytic throughput on its own.
plan.baseline_assumption: Catalysis exclusively from the substrate-bound enzyme state is treated as having no high-substrate loss of activity beyond ordinary Michaelis saturation.
plan.scientific_mechanism: A second, nonproductive substrate interaction at high substrate concentration causes classical substrate inhibition, reducing the fraction of catalytically competent substrate-bound enzyme without changing the reversible competitive binding of inhibitor at the active site.
plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the parent's idealization that substrate only activates catalysis and never inhibits it. The parent predicts a monotone increase of v_inh with S toward an asymptote for every such condition because substrate only relieves competition and fills the catalytic complex. A child with substrate inhibition instead predicts that after an initial rise, further increases in S can flatten the curve more strongly or decrease the rate, with the contrast most visible when the substrate-inhibition scale lies within or somewhat above the sampled S range. This changes the scored input-to-rate mapping itself, not merely an auxiliary quantity. A single refit of the parent cannot reproduce both ordinary Michaelis-like ascent at low S and a genuine high-S downturn at the same fixed I because its S dependence is structurally monotone. The mechanism is scientifically admissible in initial-rate enzyme assays and remains nonnegative and finite when implemented with a standard inhibitory denominator factor.

contract.assumption_after: A second substrate can bind nonproductively at high S, lowering catalytic competence and adding classical substrate inhibition on top of competitive inhibition.
contract.before_fragment: Vmax*S/(Km*(1 + ((I/(Ki + beta*I))*(1 + alpha*I/(Ki + I + S)))) + S)
contract.after_fragment: Vmax*S/(Km*(1 + ((I/(Ki + beta*I))*(1 + alpha*I/(Ki + I + S)))) + S + S**2/Ksi)
contract.parent_reduction: The successor reduces to the parent in the limit Ksi -> oo, or approximately whenever all sampled substrate concentrations satisfy S << Ksi so that S**2/Ksi is negligible.
contract.observable_signature: For fixed Ki and low-to-moderate I, sweeping S from below Km to well above it can produce a bend from rise to flattening or downturn in v_inh; the parent cannot do this because its response to S is monotone increasing for every fixed inhibitor condition. The new effect is strongest when S**2/Ksi becomes comparable to Km*(1 + ((I/(Ki + beta*I))*(1 + alpha*I/(Ki + I + S)))) + S.
contract.shortcut_blocked: A single parent parameter set cannot reproduce both ordinary low-S ascent and a genuine high-S decline at the same fixed I and Ki, because the parent denominator is affine in S outside the saturating competition modulation and therefore yields a structurally monotone increasing rate with S. Retuning Vmax, Km, alpha, beta, or Ki can shift slope and saturation scale but cannot create the added high-S suppressive curvature or bell-shaped profile.

range_suggestions.Ksi: comparable to or above the upper sampled substrate range; choose so that S**2/Ksi is negligible at low S but becomes comparable to Km + S in the high-substrate regime
